evals.name: pure linear chain plans one ticket per wave, all serial
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/linear-demo/ — the ticket set is 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02). The parent spec.md names a single eval-harness test seam for the whole feature, and each ticket has one acceptance criterion. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Wave 0 = {01}, wave 1 = {02}, wave 2 = {03} — each ticket is blocked only by the previous one, so no two tickets share a wave. The Plan's wave table shows, per ticket, its estimated touch-set, a serial disposition with the reason (blocked by the prior ticket), no overlap flag, the eval-harness test seam, and the retry budgets MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3 and MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3. There is a wave table and no model column. Stage 0 stops for explicit approval without writing to any source file.
expectations: Assigns waves 0, 1, 2 to 01, 02, 03 respectively, derived from the Blocked by edges
Marks every ticket serial because each depends on the previous ticket, with no overlap flag
Shows wave, touch-set, disposition, test seam, and retry budgets per ticket in the wave table, with no model column
Pauses for explicit approval and creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/linear-demo/

evals.name: a same-wave pair the user chose to serialize is dispatched one at a time, not concurrently
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/serialize-choice-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None), both estimated to modify src/reports/list.ts and flagged likely-overlapping — consider serializing. At Plan approval the user chooses to serialize the {01, 02} pair rather than run them in parallel. Stage 1 begins.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator honors the user's choice to serialize the flagged pair: it reuses one worktree slot at a time, in ticket-number order — dispatching, verifying, and integrating ticket 01 before starting ticket 02's worker — even though both landed in wave 0 as independent tickets and the Plan would otherwise propose running them in parallel. This differs from an unflagged independent pair, which the Plan proposes running concurrently by default.
expectations: Recognizes the user's Plan-approval choice to serialize the flagged {01, 02} pair
Reuses one worktree slot at a time for 01 and 02, in ticket-number order, rather than dispatching both concurrently
Starts ticket 02's worker only after ticket 01 reaches a terminal state
Contrasts this with an unflagged independent pair, which the Plan proposes running in parallel by default

States plainly that the retry rule is chosen by failure type — verification failure resumes, opencode-process failure never does

evals.name: a ticket escalating to fallback integrates on its own without blocking already-passed wave-mates
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/wave-fallback-demo/ — wave 1 has three independent tickets (04, 05, 06). Tickets 04 and 06 pass verification on the opencode path; ticket 05 exhausts its main-path budget and escalates to the fallback tier, which takes noticeably longer than 04 and 06.
evals.expected_output: Tickets 04 and 06 are squash-merged onto the integration branch as soon as each passes verification, in ascending ticket-number order relative to what's already integrated, each with the full suite run on that result — neither waits for ticket 05's fallback subagent to finish. Ticket 05 escalates to the fallback tier instead of integrating there, and integrates the same way once the fallback subagent's result passes the same verification gate, cut from whatever integration HEAD exists at that point (which already includes 04 and 06's work).
expectations: Squash-merges 04 and 06 as soon as each clears verification, independent of ticket 05's fallback escalation
Runs the full suite on each of 04 and 06's integrated results without waiting on 05
Escalates 05 to the fallback tier rather than blocking 04 and 06's integration on it
Integrates 05 the same way once fallback-verified, cut from the HEAD that already includes 04 and 06

evals.name: the next wave waits until every ticket in the current wave reaches a terminal state
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/wave-boundary-demo/ — wave 0 has two tickets, 01 and 02. Ticket 01 has already integrated. Ticket 02 is still inside the fallback tier, not yet integrated or BLOCKED. Wave 1's tickets are all blocked only by wave-0 tickets.
evals.expected_output: Wave 1 does not start. Even though 01 has already integrated, the orchestrator waits until 02 reaches a terminal state — integrated or BLOCKED — before dispatching any wave-1 ticket. The wave boundary gates only the start of the next wave, never 01's own already-completed integration.
expectations: Does not dispatch any wave-1 ticket while 02 has not yet reached a terminal state
Waits for 02 specifically, even though its wave-mate 01 already integrated
Treats integrated and BLOCKED as the only terminal states that satisfy the wave boundary
States that the wave boundary gates only the next wave's start, never an individual ticket's own integration

evals.name: --opencode-only suppresses fallback the same way --no-fallback did
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement --opencode-only .scratch/opencode-only-demo/ — same as escalate-demo: ticket 01 fails the verification gate three times on the main opencode path, exhausting MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS.
evals.expected_output: --no-fallback remains the primary flag name; --opencode-only is its current alias (the guarantee it names no longer has anything to do with 'local' now that the main path runs on a resolved hosted model). Under --opencode-only the orchestrator suppresses the subagent fallback the same way --no-fallback always did: ticket 01 becomes BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) directly off the main path's own exhausted budget, instead of escalating. The run spends zero Claude tokens and no code leaves the machine.
expectations: Recognizes --no-fallback as the primary suppression flag, with --opencode-only as its current alias and --strict-local as a deprecated alias
Suppresses the subagent fallback so the main path's own exhausted MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS budget yields BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) instead of escalating, exactly as --no-fallback did
Spends no Claude tokens and sends no code off the machine

evals.name: --strict-local still works as a deprecated alias for --no-fallback
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement --strict-local .scratch/strict-local-demo/ — same as opencode-only-demo: ticket 01 fails the verification gate three times on the main opencode path, exhausting MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS.
evals.expected_output: --strict-local is a deprecated alias of --no-fallback (whose current alias is --opencode-only), kept working for one release rather than removed outright: the orchestrator treats it identically, suppressing the fallback tier so ticket 01 becomes BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) rather than escalating. Nothing about the outcome differs from using --no-fallback directly.
expectations: Accepts --strict-local as a working, deprecated alias of --no-fallback rather than rejecting it
Suppresses the fallback tier identically to --no-fallback / --opencode-only
Produces BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) instead of escalating

evals.name: the resolved model is recorded in status.md and shown in the Plan
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/model-record-demo/ — no --model flag given at invocation. The model-resolution check before wave 0 resolves to deepseek/v4.1-flash-hosted.
evals.expected_output: Before wave 0 starts, the orchestrator writes the resolved model deepseek/v4.1-flash-hosted into status.md as the pinned resolved model, and the same value appears in the Plan that is presented for approval — not a guess, a fact read back from opencode models. Every worker dispatched afterward, in every wave, carries this same value as an explicit --model flag.
expectations: Records the resolved model deepseek/v4.1-flash-hosted in status.md before wave 0 starts
Shows the same resolved model in the Plan presented for approval
Treats the resolved model as a fact confirmed via opencode models, not an assumption

evals.name: tokens.main accumulates across main-path tickets and is shown in the Plan, status.md, and the handoff alongside tokens.fallback
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/tokens-main-demo/ — three tickets (01, 02, 03) each build and integrate on the main opencode path, spending real tokens against the resolved model deepseek/v4.1-flash-hosted; no ticket escalates to the fallback tier.
evals.expected_output: As each of 01, 02, and 03 clears verification and integrates, its opencode usage is added to the running cumulative tokens.main in status.md — the main path is no longer 'cost: 0'. The status report shows the accumulated tokens.main alongside tokens.fallback (zero, since nothing escalated), and the completion handoff prints the same tokens.main total as real spend against the resolved model, next to tokens.fallback.
expectations: Accumulates tokens.main across all three main-path tickets as each one integrates
Shows the accumulated tokens.main in status.md alongside tokens.fallback
Shows the same tokens.main total, as real spend, in the completion handoff alongside tokens.fallback

evals.name: a BLOCKED ticket's independent later wave is reported as an available partial path, not started automatically
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/wave-partial-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (None), 02 (None), 03 (01), 04 (02). Wave 0 = {01, 02}; wave 1 = {03, 04}. Ticket 01 becomes BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) after its fallback also fails. Ticket 02 passes and integrates.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 03 is not started — it is transitively blocked by 01. Wave 1 as a whole does not start automatically even though ticket 04 depends only on 02 (already integrated): the orchestrator reports wave 1's independent ticket 04 as an available partial path it could dispatch, but does not start it without the user resuming via /opencode-implement continue wave-partial-demo. 02 stays integrated.
expectations: Does not start ticket 03, transitively blocked by the BLOCKED ticket 01
Does not auto-start ticket 04 even though its only blocker (02) already integrated
Names ticket 04 in the halt report as an independent, available partial path rather than dispatching it
Keeps 02 integrated and ends the halt report with the /opencode-implement continue command

evals.name: /opencode-implement list reports one line per run: slug, integration branch, tickets done/total, and running/blocked/complete
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement list — three runs exist under .scratch/: subtitle-preferences (2 of 4 tickets integrated, still running), partial-demo (2 of 4 integrated, one BLOCKED), handoff-demo (4 of 4 integrated).
evals.expected_output: list prints one line per run, unchanged in shape from before this feature: subtitle-preferences — opencode-implement/subtitle-preferences — 2/4 — running; partial-demo — opencode-implement/partial-demo — 2/4 — blocked; handoff-demo — opencode-implement/handoff-demo — 4/4 — complete. It reads every .scratch/*/status.md and mutates nothing.
expectations: Prints exactly one line per discovered run
Each line names the slug, the integration branch, and tickets done/total
Each line states whether the run is running, blocked, or complete
Mutates no file while listing
